+import heapq
+
+
+def dependency_order(graph):
+    if not graph:
+        return []
+    prereqs = {}
+    for node, deps in graph.items():
+        prereqs.setdefault(node, set())
+        for dep in deps:
+            prereqs.setdefault(dep, set())
+            if dep == node:
+                raise ValueError("cycle detected: self-edge on %r" % (node,))
+            prereqs[node].add(dep)
+    dependents = {n: [] for n in prereqs}
+    indegree = {}
+    for node, deps in prereqs.items():
+        indegree[node] = len(deps)
+        for dep in deps:
+            dependents[dep].append(node)
+    heap = [n for n, d in indegree.items() if d == 0]
+    heapq.heapify(heap)
+    order = []
+    while heap:
+        node = heapq.heappop(heap)
+        order.append(node)
+        for child in dependents[node]:
+            indegree[child] -= 1
+            if indegree[child] == 0:
+                heapq.heappush(heap, child)
+    if len(order) != len(prereqs):
+        raise ValueError("cycle detected")
+    return order

action.summary: Implemented dependency_order in solution.py using Kahn's algorithm with a min-heap: builds a fresh prerequisite map (deduplicating edges via sets, including prerequisite-only nodes, never mutating input), raises ValueError on self-edges immediately and on any remaining cycle (including disconnected ones) when the emitted order is shorter than the node count, returns [] for empty input, and always pops the lexicographically smallest eligible node.
